clue.text: They can't recall, thus must enter made-up names

indicators.note: one word must enter another, so it goes inside the shuffled letters
made-up means invented, so the letters of names are put together in a new order

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: A writer warns that a story's invented names must carry a note marking them as intentional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made-up' signals the anagram and 'enter' the insertion; 'thus' is the Latin word printers use to flag a quotation copied as found.
explanation.definitionFit: People suffering memory loss, who cannot recall the past, are amnesiacs, here in the shorter spelling.

clue.text: To boot ball, wingers drop off like this

indicators.note: the wingers are the outside letters of ball, and they drop off leaving the centre

parts.note: so means in this way, as in 'do it so'

explanation.surface: A football manager tells players to kick the ball while the wide men fall back, demonstrating how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To boot' looks like kicking, but it is the definition: 'to boot' means in addition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'to boot' means moreover or as well, which is a synonym of the adverb.

clue.text: Kiss cheek

definitions.meaning: to kiss and cuddle amorously, as a verb in informal speech
cheek means impudence or nerve, as in 'what a nerve'

explanation.surface: A peck on the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are informal: snogging is necking, and brass nerve or impudence is also called by this word.

clue.text: Side wearing skirts of sky blue

indicators.note: the side is dressed in the skirts, so it goes between them
the skirts are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of sky are taken

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A team kitted out in sky-blue skirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like part of a colour, sky blue, but it is the definition in its sense of risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in the sense of smutty or erotic matches a steamy scene, both meaning sexually charged.

clue.text: Mate to talk glibly about one man's best friend?

parts.note: cocker is old British slang for mate, a form of address like 'all right, cocker?'

indicators.note: the patter goes about the word for one, holding it inside

parts.note: to spiel is to talk smoothly and at length, like a salesman
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A smooth talker chats up a friend of one of the lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the insertion. 'Mate' is a northern British form of address. The question mark is there because the definition gives this breed only as an example of a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog is called man's best friend, and this gun-dog breed is one example of a dog.

clue.text: Throws out European — company has no union

indicators.note: the guests have no union, so the letter for it is taken out

parts.note: having company means having guests round

explanation.surface: A firm on the Continent sacks staff because it refuses to recognise trade unions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' suggests a firm but means visitors here.
explanation.definitionFit: To egest is to discharge waste from the body, so the verb is a technical synonym for expelling.

clue.text: Tremendous performance against Conservative

parts.note: a gig is a live music performance
anti means against or opposed
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative, the UK party

explanation.surface: A rave review for a show that took on the Tory party.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of enormous size, so the adjective is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Work with spirit level in America

parts.note: in Britain a short is a small measure of spirits such as whisky
Americans spell the floor of a building without the E that British storey has

explanation.surface: A DIY job with a spirit level in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: A spirit level is a builder's tool, but the two words split apart and are clued separately; in British pubs a measure of whisky or gin is called a short.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief piece of fiction is a literary work, so the definition gives a category that it belongs to.

clue.text: Did butter and spread food pastes

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so the letters of food pastes are laid out anew

explanation.surface: Someone buttered the bread and spread food pastes on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' and 'spread' suggest a kitchen; 'Did butter' means flattered, as in buttering someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To butter someone up is to flatter them, and the soft-soap idiom has that same meaning of coaxing with flattery.

clue.text: You can't have a go at this bloody bully after school turned around

definitions.text: You can't have a go at this

indicators.note: turned means the abbreviation for around is read backwards

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means around a date
bloody means red with blood
to cow is to intimidate or bully

explanation.surface: A violent bully once lived after a school turned its ways around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the abbreviation for circa; 'after' looks like an order instruction but the pieces simply run in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: An institution beyond criticism, which nobody is allowed to attack, is described by this idiom from the Hindu reverence for cattle.

clue.text: Cleaner wrong? Has wiped bum

indicators.note: bum is British slang for bad or poor quality, so the letters are put wrong

explanation.surface: A cleaner has made a mess of wiping someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like a body part but is British slang for bad, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The detergent used in a laundry is a cleaning product, so the definition names its general type.

clue.text: Turn and depart

definitions.meaning: to turn is to go sour, as milk does
to leave, as in a bomb or alarm going away or a person setting out

explanation.surface: Swivel round and leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to spoil, as food does when it turns, and to leave a place.

clue.text: Does rascal show on TV small round bottom?

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child or rascal
ER is the American hospital drama series
the letter O is round
nates is the anatomical word for the buttocks

explanation.surface: Is a rascally television show of a small, round backside?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the start of a question but is the definition, in the sense of a mimic who 'does' a famous voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A mimic who 'does' a celebrity copies their voice and manner, the same as imitating them.

clue.text: Smash hit — actress is most stiff

indicators.note: to smash is to break into pieces, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A smash hit, and the actress gives a wooden performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smash hit' reads as a success, but 'Smash' is the anagram signal working on HIT ACTRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch stiffens collars, so the superlative adjective means the stiffest or most formal.

clue.text: Partners with screams: they make electricity inside

indicators.note: the power company goes inside the word for shouts

parts.note: bellows are loud shouts or roars
EDF Energy is the French-owned electricity company that supplies much of Britain

explanation.surface: Partners who scream generate electricity between them.
explanation.walkthrough: EDF Energy is a large power generator in the UK and France; 'inside' signals the insertion into the word for roars.
explanation.definitionFit: People who share a bed, or allies in a venture, are partners in the literal or figurative sense.

clue.text: Draws matches

definitions.meaning: in sport, games ending level are drawn games
fixtures in a cup competition, as in FA Cup third-round games

explanation.surface: Pulls out sticks for lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football, cup fixtures are called these, and level results also are.
explanation.definitionFit: A game ending level is one sense, and a scheduled cup fixture between two teams is the other.

clue.text: Plant (iris) adapts when neglected

indicators.note: something neglected falls into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant such as an iris adapts when it is not looked after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iris' looks like the plant, but the definition is 'Plant'.
explanation.definitionFit: This hardy leafy houseplant is famously tolerant of neglect, which is exactly why it suits the clue.

clue.text: A sign for Underground by end of station like Paddington

parts.note: a means per, as in 'once a year'
U is the sign of the Berlin U-Bahn underground railway
via means by way of

indicators.note: the end of station is its last letter

explanation.surface: Signs for the Tube at the end of Paddington station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddington' looks like the London station, but it is the bear from darkest Peru in the children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington Bear came to London from Peru, so he is a native of that South American country.

clue.text: Real gunfire shot having taken turn here?

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: a U-turn, so the letter U stands for turn

explanation.surface: Real gunfire, having had a go at shooting here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having taken' removes U (from U-turn) from the letters of REAL GUNFIRE, and 'shot' shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where people take turns to fire at targets is the shooting venue, so 'here' points to the location.

clue.text: Send back partially defrosted fish

indicators.note: the run of letters is sent back, read right to left
only part of the word defrosted is used

explanation.surface: A diner returns fish that is only half defrosted.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide, a freshwater carp-family fish often kept in garden ponds, is also called by this name.

clue.text: Old money from film copies circulating

indicators.note: the letters circulate, the front ones moving round to the back

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film about an extraterrestrial
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: Old banknotes from a film are being circulated in copied form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' moves ETA from the front of ETAPES to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain's currency was replaced by the euro in 2002, so it is an example of former money.

clue.text: Enough! Nearly calling off trip on this

indicators.note: off means wrong or bad, so the letters are rearranged
nearly means not quite all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Enough! A drug-taker almost cancels a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly calling' gives CALLIN, which is shuffled with ENOUGH. 'trip' is drug slang for a psychedelic experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Drugs like LSD produce a psychedelic experience, a trip, so the substance is what someone trips on.

clue.text: Kiss while under piece of mistletoe now?

indicators.note: in a down answer, the word for while sits under the letter from mistletoe

parts.note: X is the cross for a kiss at the end of a letter

indicators.note: a piece of mistletoe here is its first letter

parts.note: as means while, as in 'as I was leaving'

explanation.surface: A kiss under the mistletoe at this time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'under' puts AS beneath M. The question mark shows 'now' only holds at a certain time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissing under mistletoe happens at the Christmas season, so the festival is 'now' when you do it.

clue.text: Locals concerned with Poles

parts.note: in means involved or concerned with, as in 'in shipping'
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Residents concerned about Polish neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locals' suggests residents, but in Britain your local is your nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a person's local is their regular neighbourhood pub, so pubs are locals.

clue.text: Tablet reduced abdominal pain — possible cause?

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: colic is severe pain in the abdomen

explanation.surface: A pill eased stomach pain: is that what caused it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tablet' looks like medicine, but it is E, slang for an ecstasy pill.
explanation.definitionFit: The bacterium is a frequent cause of food poisoning, whose symptoms include stomach cramps.

clue.text: Bloke that is special lover?

parts.note: a lad is a bloke, an informal word for a man
i.e. abbreviates id est, meaning that is
man in the sense of boyfriend, as in 'her man'

explanation.surface: A chap who is a particularly good lover.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a bloke who is a special lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser or charmer who enjoys female company is a man popular with women, the very kind of lover described.

clue.text: Drink neat rum when touring island

indicators.note: the shuffled letters tour around the island, enclosing it
rum means strange or odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Drinking neat rum on a tour around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but means odd, the anagram signal; 'touring' wraps TANE, the shuffled letters, round the island abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal infusion is a type of drink, so the definition names a general category it belongs to.

clue.text: State two answers: scores missing first rounds

indicators.note: rounds means goes around, enclosing the answers
the first letter of the word for scores is missing

parts.note: marks are scores in a test
ANS and A are both abbreviations for answer

explanation.surface: A quiz state: two answers given, but the scores lack the opening rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' looks like quiz rounds but means surrounds: ARKS goes round ANS + A.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is a state in the southern United States, so the definition names its category.
